TITLE: RWE Q3 2026: trading lifts the year, 2027 is the next test
QUOTE: We have delivered a strong financial performance in the first nine months of 2026. … we have already achieved around 85% of our full year adjusted EPS target.
QUOTE_WHO: Michael Müller, CFO, Q3 2026 earnings call, 11 November 2026 (initial draft transcript)
COMPANY_INTRO: RWE generates electricity from offshore and onshore wind, solar, batteries and gas plants in Europe and the US, and runs a global energy trading business. Listed in Frankfurt; market value around EUR 44bn.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Beat
TAKEAWAYS.text: Adjusted EBITDA EUR 4.58bn, 3% above consensus; adjusted net income EUR 1.85bn, 8% above.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Reaction
TAKEAWAYS.text: Shares up 2.1% on 11 November, DAX about +1%: a measured response to a trading-led beat.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Outlook
TAKEAWAYS.text: 2026 now seen at the upper end; 85% of the EUR 2.6 to 3.3 EPS range already earned.

TAKEAWAYS.label: Valuation
TAKEAWAYS.text: 17.7x forward earnings, 21% above the 2014 to 2026 average, below the 21.6x May peak.

H_P1: Earnings, not the multiple, carry the stock
P1_PARAGRAPH: Adjusted EBITDA beat the company-collected consensus by 3% and adjusted net income by 8%, and the shares rose 2.1% on 11 November against a DAX up about 1%: an aligned but measured reaction. The beat came mostly from trading, which management does not extrapolate, while renewables grew on new capacity and normal wind. The quarter confirms the earnings path.
C1_TITLE: RWE: 9M 2026 adjusted net income vs. consensus and prior year
C1_SUB: Adjusted net income, EUR m · consensus: company-collected poll · 9M 2025 derived from the reported +42.8% growth
C1_COMMENT: Adjusted net income rose 43% to EUR 1,846m, EUR 137m above consensus. Trading alone added about EUR 390m of EBITDA year on year, so the beat is of lower quality than the headline. Offshore wind and onshore wind and solar each grew 21%: that is the recurring part of the story.
BASE_CASE: The case remains constructive, with a balanced to positive risk/reward at 17.7x forward earnings. We underwrite adjusted EPS at the top of the EUR 2.6 to 3.3 range for 2026 and growth beyond it from 4.5 gigawatts of offshore wind under construction, 2.5 gigawatts of contracted gas plants and batteries with returns above 10%. The debate has moved to the 2027 base once trading normalises. The next tests are the second German capacity auction in December and the 2027 guidance in early March.
UPSIDE: A second German auction award from the 1.5 gigawatt pipeline; a 2027 guide above consensus in March; one of the two data centre site deals signed by year end.
DOWNSIDE: A 2027 guide below consensus as trading falls back to its EUR 300m normal level; Sofia offline beyond year end; year-end net debt well above EUR 12bn.
H_A1: Results: trading beat, wind delivered growth
A1_PARAGRAPHS: Adjusted EBITDA rose 35% to EUR 4.6bn. Offshore wind grew to EUR 1,110m from EUR 915m on normalised wind and the ramp-up of Sofia, Thor and Nordseecluster A. Onshore wind and solar rose to EUR 1,497m from EUR 1,242m on new capacity and better European wind, despite a weaker US dollar. Flexible generation delivered EUR 1,343m, helped by higher margins, UK capacity payments and a one-off EUR 332m compensation from the Dutch state for the 2022 Eemshaven restriction. Supply and trading recovered from first-quarter losses on gas and CO2 positions to EUR 543m, against EUR 150m a year earlier. Adjusted EPS rose 42% to EUR 2.52.

Surprise and reaction are aligned: an 8% beat on adjusted net income met a 2.1% rise on 11 November, about one point better than the DAX. The reasons the move stayed measured are confirmed in the release and the call: guidance was confirmed at the upper end rather than raised, the Eemshaven payment is a one-off, and management keeps EUR 300m as the normal trading result, so the trading swing is not extrapolated. We think positioning also played a part: the stock had rerated to 21.6x in May and entered the print 39% higher over twelve months.
H_A2: Outlook: upper end now, 2027 is the question
A2_PARAGRAPH: RWE confirmed its 2026 ranges and now expects the upper end: adjusted EBITDA EUR 5.75bn to 6.35bn, adjusted net income EUR 1.95bn to 2.45bn and adjusted EPS EUR 2.6 to 3.3, with the EUR 1.32 dividend confirmed. The CFO said the guide assumes average fourth-quarter wind and excludes the strong trading seen in the quarter, while the other segments should land around their midpoints. Net debt of EUR 17bn at September should fall to around EUR 12bn by December as the Vanguard projects are deconsolidated after the KKR joint venture. Commodity assumptions have not been updated; new price sensitivities and 2027 guidance come with the full-year results in early March.
H_C2: Valuation: earnings did the work this year
C2_TITLE: RWE: share price vs. consensus earnings and valuation
C2_SUB: RWE GY Equity, weekly, Sep 2014 to 11 Nov 2026 · BEst 12m-forward consensus · 40-week simple MA · log scale · P/E shaded above (orange) / below (blue) its 2014 to 2026 average · last point is the 11 November (results day) level
C2_COMMENT: Over twelve months the share price rose 39% and consensus 12m-forward EPS 38%: the rerating has paused and earnings growth now does the lifting. Since the half-year results in August, EPS has risen 7% while the price is up 1%, taking the P/E down from 18.9x to 17.7x. The multiple stands 21% above its 14.6x average since 2014, but below the 19.1x one-year average and the 21.6x peak of May 2026. The price sits 4% above its 40-week moving average of EUR 57.1. A 10% EPS upgrade at an unchanged price would take the multiple to 16.1x.
SOURCE_LINE: Source: Syz Research, Bloomberg, company filings, RWE release and Q3 2026 earnings call of 11 November 2026
